questions.q: What triggers a record-triggered flow to run?
options: A record being created, updated, or deleted
questions.explain: A record-triggered flow runs automatically when a record is created, updated, or deleted — no user or screen involved.

questions.q: Which Configure Start setting chooses between before-save and after-save behavior?
questions.explain: Optimize the Flow For is where you choose Fast Field Updates (before-save) or Actions and Related Records (after-save).

questions.q: What can a before-save (Fast Field Updates) flow do?
options: Update fields on the record that triggered it
questions.explain: Fast Field Updates can only update fields on the triggering record itself — nothing else.

questions.q: Why is a before-save flow meaningfully faster than the after-save alternative?
options: It updates the triggering record in memory before it saves, instead of saving and re-saving it
It always runs on a schedule instead of a trigger
It only works on custom objects
questions.explain: A before-save flow updates the record before it's committed, avoiding the extra save cycle an after-save update requires.

questions.q: A flow needs to send an email whenever a Case is closed. Which option should it use?
options: Fast Field Updates, because email is always faster this way
Actions and Related Records, because sending an email requires an Action, which before-save can't run
Neither option supports sending email from a flow
Fast Field Updates, because emails don't count as Actions
questions.explain: Sending an email is an Action, and before-save (Fast Field Updates) flows cannot run Actions — that requires after-save.
